stepanyants-krapivsky-hartle-krioukov-la.why: The mathematics matches the record's Theorem 1, and the proof text follows the record's proof verbatim. The problem is the verification tag. stepanyants-krapivsky-hartle-krioukov-la.statement: [campaign result 2026-09-14, author checked; tested by direct Monte Carlo simulation of the Poisson-weighted infinite tree (4000 replicates, k=2,5,10,12), agreeing with the recursion within about 1.5 standard errors] This is the campaign's branching-walk identification behind Conjecture 1 of H. Stepanyants, P. L. Krapivsky, H. Hartle and D. Krioukov, The rank and layer distributions in random recursive trees, arXiv:2608.04303. Let the Poisson-weighted infinite tree have root position zero, with children of each vertex at the points of an independent rate-one Poisson process on (0,infinity), translated by their parent's position. Let M_k be the minimum position of generation k, and set M_0=0. Define s_0(y)=1 for y>=0 and s_k(y)=1-exp(-integral_0^y s_{k-1}(z)dz) for k>=1. Put bar_ell_k=integral_0^infinity s_k(y)exp(-y)dy and ell_k=bar_ell_k-bar_ell_{k+1}. In the source, ell_k is the limiting fraction of vertices in layer k of a random recursive tree, formed by joining each new vertex j uniformly to one of vertices 1,...,j-1. Layer zero consists of the initial leaves, and subsequent layers are obtained by successive leaf removals. For every k>=0 and y>=0, s_k(y)=P(M_k<=y). Consequently bar_ell_k=E[exp(-M_k)] and ell_k=E[exp(-M_k)-exp(-M_{k+1})]. This is an unrefereed campaign result.

stepanyants-krapivsky-hartle-krioukov-la.why: This states the record's Theorem 3 at its full strength: the limits of both normalized tails, with C* = E[exp(-M*)] defined through Aïdékon's distributional limit. It is correctly framed as a proof of Conjecture 1 conditional on the cited Addario-Berry–Ford and Aïdékon theorems. The proof text reproduces the record's Theorems 2 and 3 and their proofs without added steps. The recursion control in the tag is relevant here, because the record's numerics bear on b_k.

stepanyants-krapivsky-hartle-krioukov-ma.why: The mathematical content matches the record's Theorem 4: the layer half only, with the rank half explicitly left open, and L_n = floor(diam/2) plus the convention caveat. The proof text follows the record. Two problems. First, the verification tag cites the recursion-integration control, which has no bearing on this result. The record's check for Theorem 4 is the brute-force leaf-stripping test (h0019_layer_identity.py): 40 random recursive trees of sizes 6 to 120 and 480 vertices, plus a 5-vertex path as a control. Second, the assumption 'Rate-independent random recursive tree attachment' is not language the record uses; it should just say uniform attachment. Corrected statement below.
stepanyants-krapivsky-hartle-krioukov-ma.statement: [campaign result 2026-09-14, author checked; the combinatorial identities (layer = second-largest branch height, maximum layer = floor(diam/2) <= height) were verified by brute-force leaf stripping on 40 random recursive trees of sizes 6 to 120 (480 vertices), with the 5-vertex path as a control] This is the layer part of the campaign answer to Conjecture 2 of H. Stepanyants, P. L. Krapivsky, H. Hartle and D. Krioukov, The rank and layer distributions in random recursive trees, arXiv:2608.04303. For each integer n>=3, let T_n be a random recursive tree on vertices 1,...,n, in which each vertex j>=2 chooses its parent independently and uniformly from 1,...,j-1. Repeatedly remove all vertices of degree at most one, assigning layer zero to the first removed set and successively increasing the layer. Let L_n be the maximum layer. As n tends to infinity, L_n=e log n-(3/2)log log n+O_P(1), where logarithms are natural and O_P(1) means that the centered sequence is bounded in probability. Under this removal rule, L_n=floor(diameter(T_n)/2); other conventions for the last vertex left standing change the maximum by at most one. The proof uses the recursive-tree height estimate of Addario-Berry and Ford (Corollary 1.3) and the fact that the root's normalized subtree sizes have a stick-breaking limit whose second-largest term is positive almost surely. The maximum-rank part of Conjecture 2 is not addressed. This is an unrefereed campaign result.
